speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of bleeding, easy bruising, and joint swelling, I suspect an inherited coagulopathy like hemophilia. Do you have a personal history of prolonged bleeding after other surgeries or dental work, and have you ever experienced spontaneous joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: PT, aPTT, Factor VIII and IX levels.
The combination of persistent mucosal bleeding, easy bruising, and a family history of joint swelling is highly suggestive of a coagulation factor deficiency, likely Hemophilia A or B.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin Time (PT): 15 sec; Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT): 60 sec; Factor VIII and IX levels: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your Factor VIII and IX levels are normal but aPTT is prolonged, I need to rule out a platelet function disorder or von Willebrand disease. Have you ever experienced heavy menstrual bleeding if female, or nosebleeds, and does your family history follow an X-linked pattern? REQUEST TEST: Von Willebrand factor antigen and activity, Platelet count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Von Willebrand factor antigen: Elevated; Von Willebrand factor activity: Decreased; Platelet count: 160,000/mm3

speaker: Doctor
text: The discrepancy between elevated vWF antigen and decreased activity, along with the prolonged aPTT and family history, strongly points to von Willebrand Disease Type 2. DIAGNOSIS READY: Von Willebrand Disease
